correctness.rationale: Each unoriented direction is assigned to exactly one opposite-vertex edge pair, with angular sector bounded by its endpoint interior angles. On the sector the width is side length times cosine; a change of variable yields the exact acute/right/obtuse densities. The aggregate square-root singularity weights are 6/4/2 respectively, distinguishing angle class. For obtuse triangles the only inverse-square-root singularity gives the longest side; the minimum width gives its altitude; the two remaining altitudes are exactly the locations of strictly negative finite density jumps. Area-times-altitude identities recover the other sides, including coincident jump levels. Tested 24 triangle shapes against 140000 direct directions times 75 thresholds each, numerical PDF quadrature and asymptotic signatures using verify.py. Numerical checks do not prove generality; the explicit analytical sector proof does.

originality.rationale: The 2015 Kim–Yaskin–Zvavitch paper introduces projection-size distribution functions and constructs nonuniqueness for general planar symmetric convex bodies (Proposition 2), but its inspected Sections 1–3 do not classify all triangles or derive these acute/right/obtuse density jumps. Horváth reviews direction-indexed widths and difference-body determination, which does not solve direction-unlabeled inverse statistics. Related published reconstruction of tangential centrally symmetric polygons requires a common incircle and does not imply the present theorem for arbitrary triangular difference bodies. Targeted published-database comparisons found distinct triangle invariants but not the present classification; earlier specialized equivalent work is a residual risk.

value.rationale: Random unlabeled projection measurement discards the directional information normally used to reconstruct a planar convex body, and general shape classes are not identifiable from the resulting distribution. Establishing complete identifiability for the fundamental non-centrally-symmetric family of all triangles, including the obtuse regime where most side-length singularities disappear, supplies a natural full-class inverse theorem and an explicit singularity/jump reconstruction mechanism. It is more than a routine computation of one moment or a restricted toy parameter.
